F101 | api-identity-money | apps/api/src/modules/billing/billing.service.ts:274-279 + apps/api/src/config/configuration.ts:208 + apps/api/src/modules/entitlements/entitlement.service.ts:402 | A PAYING CUSTOMER CAN BE 403'd. The RevenueCat entitlement id is translated by `reverseEntitlementMap.get(raw) ?? raw` — an unmapped vendor id silently BECOMES our entitlement code. The grant is then written under that code, while `accessVerdict()` only ever asks about `this.defaultCode`. So a purchase whose RC entitlement identifier is not in REVENUECAT_ENTITLEMENT_MAP mints a live, paid grant the paywall never looks at. Config makes this likely, not hypothetical: the map DEFAULTS to a guessed pair `'premium:premium_monthly'`, and plans/payments-ideal-shape.md:196 contemplates the owner using `premium:premium` instead. | LADDER: compensates for not knowing RC's identifier at code-write time. Bedrock: the ledger is denominated in OUR vocabulary; a vendor id we cannot translate is an UNKNOWN, and minting a grant from an unknown is the same error class as `hasAccess` returning true on failure — inventing an assertion from absent information, which access-verdict.ts already rederived away one level up. Rederive: translation returns `mapped(code) | unknown(vendorId)`; `unknown` records the billing event FAILED (`unmapped_entitlement:<id>`) and rethrows so RC redelivers after the map is fixed; the legal code set is one closed declaration and `syncSubscriptionGrant` refuses anything outside it; the seeded default map value is deleted (unconfigured is unconfigured, not a guess). Red team: makes an invisible paid grant unrepresentable; still relies on the owner setting the map, but now fails LOUD (failed rows + retrying webhook) instead of a customer paying for a 403. | FIXED (D1 — owner-ratified 2026-08-02: adopt the shape) — translation is a SUM TYPE (billing/revenuecat-entitlement-map.ts): `mapped(code) | unknown(vendorId)`, no fallback. An unmapped RC id records the billing event FAILED as `unmapped_entitlement:<id>` and RETHROWS (RC redelivers); the same law now covers the TRANSFER/subscriber-fetch path, which carried the identical `?? rcId` passthrough. The guessed default map `'premium:premium_monthly'` is DELETED from configuration.ts — unconfigured means nothing translates. Parsing is STRICT and runs in the constructor, so a malformed map REFUSES BOOT (also refuses one vendor id mapping to two codes). The legal codes are one closed, derived union (default code + declared codes), exposed as `entitlementCodes`. PROOF: revenuecat-entitlement-map.spec.ts, 8 pass, incl. 'RED — an unmapped id records the event FAILED and RETHROWS' (asserts syncSubscriptionGrant NOT called, under any code) and 'an UNSET map translates nothing'. SURPRISE: billing-webhooks.spec.ts's harness defaulted entitlementMap to `''` and every test still translated — the F101 defect visible in the fixture itself; the harness now carries a real map. RESIDUAL CLOSED (owner-ruled 2026-08-03, D1-residual: PREMIUM IS THE ONLY PRODUCT, EVER). `RevenueCatEntitlementMap.parse` now REFUSES AT BOOT any entry whose `ourCode` differs from the default code, naming the offending code, the code accessVerdict() actually consults, and the single-product law. Consequence: the old 'one vendor id maps to two of our codes' check became unreachable (every surviving code IS the default) and was deleted rather than left as an untestable guard — its spec case feeds the same input and now hits the new refusal. SPEC: refusal + message content + happy path + default-code-relativity (the refusal is relative to config, not to the literal 'premium'); RED-proved by neutering the condition — 3 cases fail. | proof: entitlement.service.ts:402 reads only defaultCode; billing.service.ts:278-279 `?? rawEntitlement`; configuration.ts:208 seeded default.

F102 | api-identity-money | apps/api/src/modules/identity/auth/optional-clerk-auth.guard.ts:9 + apps/api/src/modules/entitlements/paywall-coverage.audit.ts:76-79 | THE BOOT AUDIT'S MARKER LIES BY OMISSION. `@BearsRequestUser()` asserts an unconditional fact, but OptionalClerkAuthGuard sets `request.user` ONLY when a token is present. The audit treats any marker-bearing guard as coverage, so a route guarded solely by OptionalClerkAuthGuard and lacking `@AllowUnentitled` PASSES boot — and then 403s every anonymous caller the moment ENTITLEMENT_GATING=enforce. That is precisely the incident class the audit exists to prevent. No live gap today (all five current OptionalClerkAuthGuard routes also carry @AllowUnentitled) — correct by discipline, not by construction. | LADDER: compensates for there being no static way to know whether a guard produces a user. Bedrock: "reachable anonymously" is a property of the ROUTE, not the guard, and guards come in three kinds, not two: always-authenticates, maybe-authenticates, never. A two-valued marker cannot express the middle one, so it rounds it to the dangerous value. Rederive: replace the boolean marker with `@AuthenticationEffect('required'|'optional'|'none')`; a route is covered iff some guard is 'required' OR it is @AllowUnentitled; an 'optional'-only route fails boot with "OptionalClerkAuthGuard admits anonymous callers — add @AllowUnentitled()". Red team: today's correct-by-luck pairing becomes unbypassable; a forgotten annotation defaults to 'none' and fails boot loudly; the only new failure is over-declaring 'optional' on a required guard, which forces a visible, harmless @AllowUnentitled. | FIXED (D2) — @AuthenticationEffect('required'|'optional'|'none') replaces the boolean marker; boot refuses an optional-only route naming it + the fix. Runtime behavior unchanged (boot-time only). PROOF: paywall-coverage.audit.spec.ts, 11 pass, incl. 'RED — an optional-only route admits anonymous callers and is reported', 'an optional-only route FAILS BOOT, naming the route and the fix', 'an optional guard PLUS @AllowUnentitled is covered, and boots'. user-bearing-guard.ts DELETED. | proof: executed spec (scratch, removed) — `bearsRequestUser(OptionalClerkAuthGuard) === true` and `uncoveredRoutes() === []` for a controller guarded only by a conditional marker-bearing guard; both assertions PASSED.

F103 | api-identity-money | apps/api/prisma/schema.prisma access_grants CHECK `access_grants_day_xor_absolute` | THE CONSTRAINT IS NAND, NOT XOR, AND THE COMMENT SAYS XOR. Live definition (verified against the local mirror): `CHECK (granted_days IS NULL OR expires_at IS NULL)` — it permits a row with BOTH null. entitlement.service.ts:108-110 documents it as "schema-enforced XOR". Both-null is how LIFETIME is spelled, so a day-grant row that lost its `granted_days` is indistinguishable from a lifetime grant: `deriveSummary` classifies `grantedDays === null` as absolute, finds `expiresAt === null`, and returns unbounded access. The emptiest possible row is the most powerful state. | LADDER: compensates for encoding three shapes in two nullable columns. Bedrock: there are three grant shapes (absolute-with-expiry, lifetime, day-count); a representation must make each one say its own name, and the accidental/empty state must be the LEAST powerful, never the most. Rederive: an explicit `kind` column ('absolute'|'lifetime'|'day') with a CHECK pinning each shape's columns exactly, so a row that sets nothing is illegal rather than immortal. A source-list-based CHECK is rejected: it would duplicate GRANT_POLICY in SQL. Red team: makes accidental-lifetime unrepresentable; costs a migration on money data; the existing code paths cannot currently produce both-null (grant() rejects days<=0 and demands expiresAt|lifetime), so this is a representation defect, not a live bug — which is exactly when it is cheap to fix. | FIXED (D3 — owner-ratified 2026-08-02) — migration 20260803020000_access_grant_kind adds `access_grants.kind` ('lifetime'|'days'|'window') with a per-kind CHECK (`access_grants_kind_shape`) pinning each shape's columns exactly; the NAND `access_grants_day_xor_absolute` is dropped. The backfill DERIVES kind from column shape (days-set→days, window-set→window, both-null→lifetime) and the migration then ASSERTS totality in a DO block — row count == classified count == count in the union, else RAISE and roll back. Code reads `kind` explicitly: deriveSummary partitions on `grant.kind`, the lifetime short-circuit tests `kind === 'lifetime'` rather than an absent expiry, and every write (grant, syncSubscriptionGrant create AND update) states its kind. APPLIED to the local mirror: comp→lifetime 2, subscription→window 2, trial_base→window 1, zero unclassified. Fresh-DB replay of all 218 migrations clean. PROOF: the DB-backed entitlement.service.spec.ts, 12 pass, incl. 'RED — a day-grant that loses its granted_days can no longer become immortal' (the DB rejects the both-null row with access_grants_kind_shape) and 'every write NAMES its shape'. | proof: `pg_get_constraintdef` on the local mirror.

F104 | api-identity-money | apps/api/src/modules/billing/billing.service.ts:184-188 | IDEMPOTENCY DEFEATED BY A FALLBACK. `externalId = event.id || original_transaction_id || transaction_id || `${Date.now()}`` — an event carrying none of the three ids gets a NEW synthetic id on every delivery, so the exactly-once check (`billingEventLog.findUnique`) can never match a replay of it, and RevenueCat's retries re-apply it. | LADDER: compensates for "the payload might not identify itself". Red team: makes silent duplicate application impossible; the new failure is rejecting a hypothetical id-less RC event, which is loud, findable, and correct. | FIXED (D4) — idempotency key = vendor event id, else a stable content hash of vendor-sent fields (billing/webhook-event-identity.ts); the Date.now() branch is deleted. PROOF: billing-webhooks.spec.ts 'an id-less event REPLAYED is applied exactly once (content-hash identity)' + MUTATION spec; mutation-verified RED — restoring`|| ${Date.now()}` makes the replay test fail with seen.size Expected 1 / Received 2 (the dup lands). | proof: read; the same file's own replay guard at :193-207 keys on this value.

F105 | api-identity-money | apps/api/src/modules/moderation/moderation.service.ts:35-43 | FAIL-OPEN MODERATION, WITH THE FIX ALREADY WRITTEN ELSEWHERE IN THE REPO. On any LLM error the decision is `{allowed:true, reason:'moderation_error'}` — a boolean return type that cannot say "I could not find out", so its catch block invents an assertion, globally, for every caller (username claims, poll/photo content). The comment concedes it and defers. | LADDER: this is verbatim the defect access-verdict.ts already rederived: three honest answers, not two. Bedrock: allowed / blocked / indeterminate; the policy for indeterminate belongs to the CALL SITE, because a username claim (retryable, cheap to refuse) and a comment post (availability wins) genuinely differ. Rederive: `ModerationVerdict = allowed | blocked(reason) | indeterminate(cause,message)` plus `resolveModeration(verdict, 'allow'|'hold')`, mirroring resolveVerdict exactly — the pattern is proven and tested in this codebase, it simply never reached moderation. Red team: makes a global lie unrepresentable; each surface must state its policy out loud; nothing changes behaviourally until a call site chooses 'hold'. | FIXED (D9 — owner-ratified 2026-08-02) — moderation-verdict.ts adopts the access-verdict shape verbatim: `allowed | blocked(reason) | indeterminate(cause,message)` plus `resolveModeration(verdict, 'allow'|'hold')`, documented in the same style and for the same reason. The catch block no longer invents `{allowed:true, reason:'moderation_error'}`; it logs the outage LOUD and returns indeterminate. ALL SEVEN call sites are WRITE paths and each states its policy out loud as `'hold'` with a per-site comment (polls: description, user-supplied entity name, poll title, discussion question, comment create, comment edit; identity: checkAvailability, which claimUsername uses as its only gate). A refusal now names its cause, so 'the text was rejected' and 'the moderator was unreachable' are distinguishable: username gained the reason `moderation_unavailable`, distinct from `profanity`. No read surface calls moderation today; 'allow' exists and is spec'd for when one does. PROOF: moderation-verdict.spec.ts, 7 pass, incl. 'RED — a moderator outage is indeterminate, NOT an allow'. | proof: read; access-verdict.spec.ts is the working precedent.

F200 | api-ops | ops-dashboard.controller.ts:41-53 (@Get page route) + ops-token.guard.ts:31 + ops-dashboard.html.ts:3,141-163 | THE OWNER'S INCIDENT CONSOLE CANNOT BE OPENED BY THE OWNER. The HTML page is served by `@Get()` under the class-level `@UseGuards(OpsTokenGuard)`, and that guard reads the `x-ops-token` HEADER only. A browser cannot attach a custom header to a top-level navigation, so `GET /ops` from a browser is a 401 in every case — with no token, with the documented `?token=` bootstrap, and with any URL a bookmark could hold. The page's own delivery machinery is therefore unreachable code: the module doc at html.ts:3 advertises "stores the ?token= in localStorage on first visit", and the `tokenGate` prompt at :152-162 is the fallback for a visit that can never happen. Only a header-capable client (curl/fetch) can fetch the page, and such a client has no use for HTML. This is the shipped consequence of a CORRECT fix applied at one level only: red team #7 removed the `?token=` branch because a query-string secret is recorded by the logging interceptor, the exception filter, Sentry, browser history and proxy logs — true, and it must not come back — but the PAGE's delivery was never rederived to match, so the surface was hardened into inaccessibility. | LADDER: the guard compensates for there being one credential mechanism for two genuinely different resources. Bedrock: the JSON routes carry DATA and are called by a header-capable client, so a header is the right credential; the PAGE carries no data at all and is fetched by a NAVIGATION, whose only credential mechanism the browser can supply automatically is a cookie. One guard cannot serve both without either leaking the secret (query) or refusing the browser (header) — which is exactly the fork this code is stuck on. Rederive: a one-time bootstrap route (`GET /ops/enter?token=…`) that validates, sets an HttpOnly+Secure+SameSite=Strict session cookie, and 302s to `/ops` WITHOUT the query string, so the secret never reaches a logged URL and never reaches JS; the page route accepts the cookie, the JSON routes accept cookie OR header; the page's localStorage token handling and tokenGate are then deleted outright (the browser holds the credential, not the document). Red team: makes "the console is unreachable in an incident" impossible and makes "the secret is in a logged URL" impossible at the same time — today's design only achieves the second. The bootstrap URL is still logged once, so it must be single-use-per-visit and the cookie short-lived; that is strictly better than every subsequent fetch carrying it. New failure: a cookie is ambient authority, so the JSON routes need the existing CSRF posture checked for the one POST (alerts ack). | FIXED (D19) | PROOF: executed Nest+Fastify probe, now PERMANENT as ops-browser-access.spec.ts (8/8 green). `GET /ops/enter?token=<correct>` => 302, Location == `/ops` carrying NEITHER the token NOR `token=`, Set-Cookie `ops_session=<expiry>.<hmac>` with HttpOnly+Secure+SameSite=Strict and NOT containing the secret; that cookie then opens BOTH `GET /ops` (200, real HTML) and `GET /ops/api/summary` (200). The three original defect assertions still hold as regression cases: naked `GET /ops` => 401, `GET /ops?token=<correct>` => 401 (the query-string secret stays dead), header => 200 UNCHANGED, and a PRESENT-but-wrong header still 401s (the cookie never widens a failed header check). OpsTokenGuard's file is byte-unchanged; OpsAccessGuard delegates to it whenever a header is present. Absent env => 404 on page, JSON and bootstrap alike. Forged, EXPIRED, and rotated-secret cookies all 401. Page's localStorage bootstrap + tokenGate DELETED — the document now holds no credential at all. NOTE FOR OWNER: `Secure` is unconditional per the binding constraint, so cookie access requires https (staging/prod); plain-http localhost must use the header path.

F202 | api-signals | signal-demand-read.service.ts (14 occurrences of `LEFT JOIN entity_redirects` + `COALESCE(r.to_entity_id, …)`) vs :608-628 lastEntityViewAt; corroborated by signal-demand-read.territory.spec.ts:145 | THE LEDGER'S IDENTITY LAW IS A CONVENTION EVERY READER MUST REMEMBER, AND ONE READER ALREADY FORGOT. Because the ledger is never rekeyed (correct, and the reason merges are cheap), "resolve subject_id through entity_redirects at read" is load-bearing for correctness — and it is enforced nowhere. It is hand-copied as a LEFT JOIN + one-hop COALESCE at 14 sites in this file alone, plus demand-mass.reader.ts and poll-ballot-mention.service.ts. `lastEntityViewAt` omits it: it filters `s.subject_id = ${entityId}` raw, so after a merge the repeat-view dedupe valve stops seeing the loser-id history. Blast today is small (a duplicate view act inside the 2-minute window), but the omission is the PROOF that nothing prevents the next, larger one — the next reader to forget could be a demand-mass path. The guard that exists is worse than none: territory.spec.ts:145 asserts `expect(demandSql).toContain('entity_redirects')`, which a reader that joins the table and then ignores the COALESCE passes, and which act-identity.ts's own header already names as the failure mode that let three SQL dialects coexist under a shared vocabulary. | LADDER: compensates for `signals`/`signal_demand_daily` exposing a RAW subject_id that is not the identity anyone wants. Bedrock: if no legitimate reader ever wants the unresolved id, the unresolved id should not be what a reader can reach — the resolution belongs to the substrate, not to each caller's memory. This is precisely the class the extraction-scope lockdown solved for events, and the same move act-identity.ts already made one level up: `dailyActsCteSql` became a BUILDER exactly because "a builder cannot be half-adopted" — yet the redirect join is still passed INTO it by each caller via the `from` parameter, so the one abstraction that closed this hole for the day-acts law deliberately left identity outside it. Rederive: a database VIEW (`signals_resolved` / `signal_demand_daily_resolved`) exposing `subject_id` already folded through the one-hop redirect, with the raw columns renamed (`raw_subject_id`) so reaching for the unresolved id is a deliberate, greppable act; every reader selects from the view, and the app-side `expandWithRedirectSources` sargability trick becomes an index on the view's predicate rather than a thing each query restates. Where a view cannot serve (the aggregate REBUILD must write raw ids), the raw table stays reachable under its own name — one place, stated. Red team: makes "a reader forgot the COALESCE" unrepresentable rather than merely untested; the `toContain` test can then be deleted rather than strengthened, because there is no fragment left to assert. New failure: a view adds a planner hop on hot autocomplete reads — must be measured against the current sargable-expansion path before adopting, and if it loses, the fallback is the weaker-but-real fix (make `dailyActsCteSql` own the redirect join instead of accepting it as a parameter, and route every non-CTE reader through a single `resolvedSubjectSql()` builder). | FIXED (D20a — the fragment-home fallback, NOT the view) | PROOF: new signals/subject-identity.ts owns `redirectJoinSql` / `resolvedSubjectSql` / `subjectMatchesSql`; all 14 hand-copied sites in signal-demand-read.service.ts converted, and the LIVE OMISSION at lastEntityViewAt fixed (it now joins and compares through `subjectMatchesSql`, so a merged loser id's history is visible again). subject-identity-lockdown.spec.ts is MUTATION-PROVEN: planting a hand-rolled `COALESCE(r.to_entity_id, s.subject_id)` + `LEFT JOIN entity_redirects` in a scratch file turned it RED naming `modules/signals/scratch-mutation-probe.ts`; probe removed, 7/7 green. The weak `toContain('entity_redirects')` assertions are gone. The VIEW was deliberately not adopted: its planner-hop cost on the hot autocomplete path is unmeasured, and F202 itself names this as its fallback.

F203 | api-signals | signals.service.ts:160-180 (record) + 7 injecting services | "RECORD THE SIGNAL" IS A CONVENTION, NOT A CHOKEPOINT — AND THE LEDGER IS THE ONE RECORD (§3). `record()` returns `void` and is called as a bare fire-and-forget statement by 7 services (search, on-demand-request, search-query-interpretation, polls, history, user-lists, signals.controller). Nothing structurally connects an ACT to its ledger row: a new surface that performs a user act simply does not call it, and the omission is invisible forever — no test fails, no metric moves, and the aggregate faithfully derives from a ledger that never heard about the act. The controller's own doc states the intended law ("every other act kind records at its own chokepoint") but "chokepoint" here means "a line of code someone remembered to write at the right place", which is the same level the codebase has repeatedly rejected elsewhere. HONESTLY: I found no MISSING writer today — the 7 sites cover the 9 declared kinds. This is a representation defect, not a live bug, which per this repo's own precedent (F103's framing) is exactly when it is cheapest to fix. | LADDER: compensates for the act and its record being two separate things a developer must pair. F204 | api-signals | integrity/sybil-cluster-report.service.ts:606 | THE ONE PLACE IN THE REPO THAT COMPARES `signals.occurred_at` WITHOUT THE COERCION THE MODULE WROTE FOR IT. `AND s.occurred_at >= now() - make_interval(days => 30)` compares a NAIVE-UTC column against a timestamptz, so Postgres coerces the right side to the SESSION time zone's wall clock. signals/sql-instant.ts exists for precisely this column and this reason, and every other consumer uses it. Measured on the local mirror (session TZ America/Chicago, `occurred_at` confirmed `timestamp without time zone`): the boundary is `2026-07-03 20:39` under Chicago vs `2026-07-04 01:39` under UTC — the sybil sweep's 30-day lookback silently slides by the server's UTC offset. Correct on a UTC box, wrong by the offset anywhere else, and the asymmetry is nasty: Prisma parses the same column back into JS as UTC (verified), so the JS-side timing math is right while the SQL-side window is skewed. | LADDER: compensates for nothing — it is a helper that nobody is FORCED to use, which is the same class as F202 one module over. Bedrock: a naive-UTC column has exactly one correct comparison form, and the module that owns the column already states it. Rederive: `AND s.occurred_at >= ${utcInstantSql(new Date(Date.now() - SWEEP_LOOKBACK_DAYS * MS_PER_DAY))}` — the import is one line. Structurally: sql-instant.ts's doc says "for signals.occurred_at, and nothing else"; a lint rule (or the existing source-scanner pattern that policed 162 columns before it was retired) keyed on the literal `occurred_at` appearing in raw SQL without `utcInstantSql` would make the omission impossible rather than merely rare — worth it precisely because there is now exactly one column left to police. | FIXED (D21) — NOTE: the one-line utcInstantSql fix had ALREADY landed at :606 under a prior pass before I arrived; what this pass added is the POLICE. | PROOF: executed on localhost/crave_search — `SHOW timezone` => America/Chicago; `pg_typeof(occurred_at)` => timestamp without time zone; the two boundary values above computed under `SET TIME ZONE` Chicago vs UTC; Prisma round-trip probe confirmed the JS side reads UTC.

F205 | api-signals + api-ops | signal-demand-aggregate.service.ts:201-207, signal-partition-maintenance.service.ts:78-86, integrity/sybil-cluster-report.service.ts:116-122 | THREE CRONS WHOSE DEATH IS INVISIBLE, ONE OF WHICH SILENTLY STOPS THE LEDGER. All three catch everything and emit a log line only; none emits an ops_alert, though OpsAlertsService is the codebase's single owner-attention seam, is already injected into the sybil service, and is described in its own doc as existing for exactly these chokepoints. The consequences are not equal and the partition one is severe: partition maintenance keeps `signals` RANGE partitions ahead of the clock, and its own header states that an insert into a month with no partition FAILS the write while the §3 law makes the writer swallow that failure — so a dead cron eventually means every signal is silently dropped, observable only as a `warn` per write and a ledger that quietly stops growing. Its comment calls the failure "loud but non-fatal"; `logger.error` with no alert is not loud, and the two-month lead means the alarm the design relies on has no bell. Aggregate refresh failing silently leaves the collector's territory read deciding what to enrich from a frozen aggregate. Sybil sweep failing silently turns the vote-integrity detector off with no indication — an always-green instrument by absence. | LADDER: each catch compensates for a real and correct law ("a background failure must not crash the process"). Bedrock: not crashing and not telling anyone are different decisions, and the second was never made — it was inherited from the first. The repo has already ratified the principle ("every metric must be able to show RED") and already built the mechanism. Rederive: each catch keeps swallowing AND calls `opsAlerts.emit({severity, kind, dedupeKey})` — `critical` for partition maintenance (it can lose user acts), `warn` for the other two, each with a dedupeKey so a persistent failure nags once rather than every tick, which the emit path already supports. Better still for the partition case, because a cron that never RUNS raises no exception to catch: assert the invariant instead of the pass — a cheap daily check that a partition covering `now + 1 month` exists, alerting on its absence, which catches a scheduler that died as well as a DDL that failed. Red team: the alert path itself can fail, and it too is fire-and-forget — so this reduces silence, it does not eliminate it; the partition-existence assertion is the one that genuinely cannot be fooled by a process that simply stopped scheduling. | FIXED (D21) | PROOF: all three catches now swallow AND emit, with day-bucketed dedupeKeys per the existing pattern — partition maintenance CRITICAL (`signal_partition_maintenance_failed:<day>`), aggregate refresh WARN, sybil sweep WARN. PLUS the un-foolable shape: `assertLeadPartitionExists()` runs daily and alerts CRITICAL when the now+1-month partition is absent, which fires on a scheduler that simply stopped as readily as on a DDL that threw. LIVE PROOF on the local mirror inside BEGIN/ROLLBACK: the assertion's exact query returned 1 with `signals_p2026_09` present, 0 after DETACH+DROP of that future partition, and 1 again after ROLLBACK (mirror untouched). Unit-proven both ways in signal-partition-maintenance.service.spec.ts (silent when present, CRITICAL when absent, WARN when the check itself throws).

F206 | api-ops | ops-summary.service.ts:253-261 (warnSwallowed) + :704-737, :777-797, :846-884 | THE INCIDENT DASHBOARD CANNOT SAY "I DON'T KNOW", SO IT SAYS ZERO. `warnSwallowed` is a good single seam and its doc states the right rule ("degrade its own card, but NEVER silently — every swallow logs"). Spec-proven: a failed Places/Sources read yields `{ok:false,reason}` and NOT `{ok:true,data:[]}`; a failed count yields `{ok:false}` while its neighbours stay `{ok:true,data:7}`; and the renderer spec asserts every pipeline cell routes through numSection and none through num().

F207 | api-signals | signal-demand-read.service.ts:1070-1078 (expandWithRedirectSources) and :1111-1118 (expandPlaceIdsWithAncestors) | TWO CATCH BLOCKS THAT CHANGE THE ANSWER, NOT THE AVAILABILITY. Both are described as pure sargability/expansion optimisations, but their fallbacks return the UNEXPANDED input: on a transient DB error `expandWithRedirectSources` drops every merged entity's history from the demand score, and `expandPlaceIdsWithAncestors` drops the ancestor rows that the read algebra's own doc calls load-bearing ("a coarse signal stored at TX reaches an Austin engine through the TX row"). Rederive: let both throw; the CALLER decides whether a demand read that cannot be computed should fail the request or be skipped this cycle — the same "policy belongs at the call site" conclusion the repo reached for moderation. If a fallback must exist, it must be visible in the RETURN (a `partial: true` flag), never only in a debug log. COLLECTOR CALL SITE FOUND at keyword-slice-selection.service.ts:245 (KeywordSliceSelectionService.selectTermsForSource -> territoryEntityDemand), and it implements skip-this-cycle-LOUDLY: logger.error + an ops alert WARN `collector_demand_read_unavailable:<sourceId>:<day>` naming the source, then rethrow. The rethrow reaches CollectorPacerService's existing per-lane catch, which leaves the lane DUE — so the cycle is skipped with no cadence advance, rather than resolving with `terms: []`, which the pacer reads as the legitimate 'nothing due' outcome. Spec keyword-slice-demand-unavailable.spec.ts proves both (2/2).

F208 | api-ops | infrastructure/throttler/throttler.decorator.ts:12,26-36,98-102,115-132 | A DECORATOR THAT DECLARES A CEILING AND APPLIES NOTHING, PLUS FOUR DEAD EXPORTS. F212 | api-signals | integrity/sybil-cluster-report.service.ts:38-40 vs :558-587 | THE COMMENT SAYS THE SWEEP IS BOUNDED; TWO OF ITS THREE QUERIES ARE NOT. `SWEEP_LOOKBACK_DAYS` is documented as "K7 plumbing — sweep lookback. Bounds the daily scan", and it bounds exactly one fetcher (`fetchIpVoteRows`). `fetchDeviceVoteClusters` joins `user_devices` to ALL of `poll_endorsements` with no time predicate, and `fetchHeavyDevices` scans all of `user_devices` — both grow without limit for the life of the product, and both re-report the same ancient clusters forever (harmless only because the ops_alerts dedupe key collapses them). Downstream, `filterToLiveEndorsements` and `leaderWithAndWithout` then issue one `pollEndorsement.findMany` PER POLL, twice over — an N+1 across an unbounded poll set. | LADDER: the constant compensates for wanting a bounded daily job; it was applied to the query it was written next to. Bedrock: "the sweep looks back N days" is a property of the SWEEP, so every fetcher it drives must honour it. Rederive: push the lookback into all three fetchers (device clusters and heavy devices bounded by endorsement/registration recency), and collapse the two per-poll endorsement loops into one keyed fetch for the whole poll set. Red team: a genuinely old ring that only votes today is still caught, because the ENDORSEMENT is recent even when the device registration is not — so bound on the act, not on the registration, or the fix creates a real blind spot. That subtlety is the reason to design this rather than patch it. | FIXED (D24) | PROOF: all three fetchers bounded, on the ACT. fetchDeviceVoteClusters adds `pe.created_at >= <cutoff>` while the multi-account-device subquery stays DELIBERATELY unbounded, so an old ring voting today is still caught — spec-asserted directly (`toContain('pe.created_at >=')`, `not.toContain('ud.first_seen')`, `not.toMatch(/ud\.last_seen\s*>=/)`). fetchIpVoteRows already carried it. DEVIATION, FLAGGED: fetchHeavyDevices is bounded on recent endorsement OR recent device activity (a UNION), because a pure endorsement bound would delete the K1 sentence's 'votes or not' trigger for a brand-new device — the union bounds the scan without narrowing what the sentence catches, and has no blind spot in either direction. The N+1 is collapsed into ONE keyed `findMany({where:{pollId:{in:[...]}}})` shared by filterToLiveEndorsements and leaderWithAndWithout via a per-sweep EndorsementIndex; spec proves 3 polls => 1 call, and the fake prisma now understands ONLY `in` so a regression cannot hide. 14/14 green.

F350 | api-places-enrichment | places-promotion.service.ts:383-398,539-551 + tomtom-chain-probe.adapter.ts:354-360,602-607 vs governance.service.ts:721-726 | "A CONSUMED DRAW" IS DEFINED THREE DIFFERENT WAYS IN ONE FLOW, AND THE TWO THAT COST MONEY DISAGREE WITH THE ONE THAT SPENDS IT. governance.drawWithOutcome debits the pool on a THROW ("we conservatively debit 1 — the request likely reached the vendor"). The adapter's `recordDraw()` (api_usage_ledger) runs ONLY after a non-null response, so a transport error writes no ledger row. The promotion service's `draws.scarce` (the CAMPAIGN ENVELOPE) is likewise never incremented on the transport-error path — while promoteOne's own docstring states it meters "promoted, consumed-draw miss, wrong-entity reject, no-rings, TRANSPORT ERROR", and the catch block's comment asserts "the draw was conservatively debited". Both claims are false of the code beside them. Consequence: on a TomTom fault the rate pool is debited, the campaign envelope is not, and cost-reconcile cannot see the draw at all — the same "summed the wrong column" class as the $118 Places lesson, one level down, and the same class as the campaign envelope that "was sized for Places spend it never debited" (round-six cost #4). | LADDER: compensates for the draw being counted at three levels that were each built at a different time, with no shared definition. Bedrock: a vendor draw is ONE event; who was charged is a property of the draw, not of the caller that noticed it. Rederive: `governance.drawWithOutcome` is the only place that knows whether the vendor was reached, so it should RETURN that fact — `{admitted, value, drawsConsumed}` — and both the ledger write and the campaign meter should hang off that single return rather than off each caller's guess. The adapter's recordDraw and the promotion service's `draws` counter then stop being independent re-derivations of a fact the governor already computed. Red team: makes under-metering unrepresentable rather than merely untested; costs a signature change at ~8 governed call sites; the new failure is OVER-metering when a request genuinely never left the process (connect-refused), which is the conservative direction the pool already chose deliberately. | FIXED (D51, owner-ruled 2026-08-03 — the metering GAP is CLOSED, in the recommendation's own shape). `governance.drawWithOutcome` now takes `onDrawConsumed` and fires it EXACTLY ONCE per ADMITTED draw — success path AND throw path, never on a denial — and the api_usage_ledger write plus the campaign envelope both hang off that single announcement instead of re-deriving 'a draw happened' from a response only the happy path has. Deleted: three post-hoc `recordDraw(op)` calls in the adapter and both manual `draws.scarce += 1` increments in the promotion service. Accepted cost, exactly as the finding's red team framed it: a connect-refused is now metered, which is OVER-metering in the conservative direction the pool already chose. A meter that throws cannot fail the draw it meters. PROOF: 4 new governance cases (announce on success, announce on throw, NOT on denial, meter-throw is swallowed) + a promotion case proving a transport-errored draw is charged to the campaign; MUTATION-PROVEN — deleting the throw-path announcement turns exactly one test RED. || PRIOR PASS: FIXED-PARTIAL (D29a accounting-truth half landed 2026-08-03) | PROOF(pass1): read all three; governance.service.ts:721-726 debits in `catch`, adapter recordDraw is after the null-check, promotion `draws.scarce += 1` appears only at :558 and :573, never in the :539 catch. || PASS-3 PROOF (D29a): the two draw words are DEFINED ONCE, in governance.drawWithOutcome's docstring — ADMITTED (pool, debits on throw) vs ANSWERED (ledger + campaign, hang off a non-null response) — and all three meters now state which they count. promoteOne's docstring no longer lists 'transport error' among metered exits; the :539 catch no longer claims a debit the ledger/campaign never made; the adapter's recordDraw says ANSWERED. Spend behaviour byte-unchanged (no call site added, removed or reordered); yarn build + full suite green.

F351 | api-places-enrichment | apps/api/src/modules/places/places-containment.integration.spec.ts:407,433 | THE ONLY DB-BACKED TEST IN THE REPO DID NOT COMPILE, AND BOTH MECHANISMS THAT SHOULD HAVE CAUGHT IT WERE DARK. This is the file whose own header says a law enforced by the database has to be proven against the database, and that it "FAILS LOUDLY without [DATABASE_URL] rather than skipping: a silently-skipped test proves nothing, which is the exact disease this file treats". It was not skipping — it was failing to compile (`new SignalDemandAggregateService(prisma, logger)` against a constructor that gained an `opsAlerts` parameter, almost certainly from the concurrent api-signals pass landing F205). It is excluded from `yarn test` by testPathIgnorePatterns, so only `yarn test:db` runs it, and only CI runs `yarn test:db` — and CI dies at the `Lint` step, which precedes both `Type check` and `test:db`, on every one of the last 6 runs. So the twelve containment laws — including the largest-gap antimeridian law that this very file proved RED twice before its fix — have been unguarded. EXECUTED: `npx tsc --noEmit` reports these two lines as the ONLY type errors in the entire API. | LADDER: compensates for nothing; it is rot admitted by a gate nobody watches. Bedrock: a guard that cannot run is not a guard, and "excluded from the default test run" plus "the only lane that runs it is behind an earlier failing step" is two independent single points of failure on the repo's most expensive-to-rebuild knowledge. Rederive: (a) run the integration lane BEFORE lint in CI, or at minimum make lint non-blocking for the test steps, so a green-tests signal cannot be hidden behind a formatting failure; (b) since `yarn type-check` DOES catch this class in one second, make type-check the first CI step; (c) better still, delete the testPathIgnorePatterns exclusion and have the spec skip-with-failure on a missing DATABASE_URL exactly as its header already promises, so `yarn test` locally surfaces the breakage the moment it happens. Red team: (a)+(b) are pure ordering with no downside; (c) makes every local `yarn test` need a database, which is a real cost — so (b) is the one I would land first, and it is free. | FIXED (test-only; production untouched) — added the missing OpsAlertsService stub argument at both call sites. PROOF: `npx jest --testPathIgnorePatterns='[]' --testRegex='places-containment.*integration'` against the local mirror now runs GREEN, 12/12, including "THE ALEUTIAN CLASS", "the UK class", "P4 DERIVED BBOX AT THE SEAM" and "THE BBOX LIES, THE GROUND JUDGES". Before the fix: "Test suite failed to run", 0 tests. The CI-ordering half remains OWNER-DECISION.

The sibling primary-enrichment queue captures it and documents exactly why ("AsyncLocalStorage does not cross the BullMQ boundary (round-six cost #4: the envelope was sized for Places spend it never debited)") — the lesson was learned in one queue and never carried to the other two. (b) The worker's entry point calls `getPlaceDetails(placeId, { includeRaw: true })` — the FULL mask — while labelling the work `attribution: 'grounding.refresh'`; `refreshStaleLocations` was deliberately built to use the lean REFRESH_PLACE_DETAILS_FIELD_MASK_FIELDS precisely so refresh polls "bill below the Enterprise+Atmosphere SKU the full mask forces". (b) compensates for two SKUs and one method; bedrock: the field mask determines the price, so "which mask" is not a call-site option, it is the identity of the operation — `getPlaceDetailsRefresh()` and `getPlaceDetailsFull()` as separate methods make a refresh that bills enterprise impossible to write. RED-proved: relabelling the spec fixture back to 'grounding.refresh' fails 2 spend-analytics cases. The CALL is byte-identical — mask unchanged, no campaign capture. || PASS-3 PROOF (F352a, owner-ruled 2026-08-03): (a) IS NOW FIXED. `currentCampaignId()` is captured into the expansion job payload and `runInWorkContext` re-established in the worker — the same mechanism the primary-enrichment and attribute-ontology lanes use, and the bulk paths that enqueue this work (city-reextract.runner:91, gemini-batch.service:676) already establish that context, so the capture is live rather than theoretical. Verified there is no gate: usage-ledger's meterCampaignSpend is post-hoc, fire-and-forget metering (:299) with no refusal path, so capture adds a bill line and an envelope drawdown, never a veto. F353 | api-places-enrichment | restaurant-location-enrichment.service.ts:2312-2448 (enrichSecondaryLocations) | THE `locationBias` PARAMETER OF SECONDARY EXPANSION IS DEAD, AND A RULED DESIGN IS BUILT ON THE BELIEF THAT IT IS LIVE. `enrichSecondaryLocations(entity, placeDetails, locationBias?)` has exactly ONE caller (:744) and it passes TWO arguments. `GooglePlacesService.findPlaceFromText` applies a bias only under `if (options.locationBias)`, so the live expansion is an UNBIASED GLOBAL text search for the brand name. plans/data-audit-2026-08.md's P2.2 research states the opposite as the cause of its class (b): "The brand is right; secondary expansion is LOCATION-BIASED so it never attached the other metro's branches" — and P2.2 rule 2 proposes spending a new per-mention Places call with the mention metro's bias to repair it. MEASURED on the local mirror, the premise does not hold: Chipotle 61 locations, Raising Cane's 58, Jet's Pizza 56, sweetgreen 39, Dunkin' 39 — all multi-metro, all one domain, all expanded. What the data DOES show is (i) 23 restaurants sit at or past the per-run cap of 60 with a maximum of 121, i.e. large brands hold an ARBITRARY, RANKING-DEPENDENT, TRUNCATED sample of their real branches (Chipotle has thousands), and (ii) a separate real class the research did not name: `Shake Shack 1700 Broadway - 53rd & 7th` has ONE location, because when Google's displayName for the grounding place is branch-qualified, the brand-purity gate `restaurantNamesAgree(canonicalName, siblingName)` rejects every genuine sibling. | LADDER: the dead parameter compensates for nothing — it is residue that makes the code READ as biased, which is how the research reached a wrong diagnosis; that is the real cost of dead code here. Bedrock, and the part that matters for the build: P2.2's metro test asks "does this brand have a location in the mention's metro?", and that question is only answerable against a COMPLETE location set. Today's set is knowingly truncated at 60-per-run and knowingly empty for branch-qualified brands, so the metro test would answer "no" for a real chain and MINT A TWIN — precisely the class-(b) failure P2.2's red team set out to avoid, reached by a different road. Rederive: before P2.2 ships, expansion must either be complete or must SAY it is incomplete — a per-brand `expansionComplete` fact (set false when a run hits the cap or the name gate rejected candidates), and the metro test must abstain (adopt, never mint) whenever it is false. The name gate should compare against the entity's BRAND name (normalizeBrandName already exists in this file) rather than Google's branch-qualified displayName. Red team: this does not weaken brand purity — an abstain is strictly safer than a mint — and it removes the need for rule 2's extra per-mention Places call in the common case, which is the cheaper answer to the same problem. | FIXED (D28 APPROVE, 2026-08-03) — the premise correction is recorded in plans/data-audit-2026-08.md:582-583 (locationBias dead; expansion global but CAP-TRUNCATED at 60); landed in c29265179 | PROOF: grep — one call site, two arguments; google-places.service.ts:637 `if (options.locationBias)`; psql on localhost/crave_search for the location counts, the 23-at-cap figure, and the Shake Shack row.

F354 | api-places-enrichment | restaurant-location-enrichment.service.ts:2442-2447 vs restaurant-secondary-location-expansion-queue.service.ts:49 | A RETRY POLICY THAT CAN NEVER FIRE, GUARDING A JOB THAT FAILS PARTWAY BY DESIGN. `enrichSecondaryLocations` wraps its entire paginated body — every Places call, every upsert — in one `catch` that logs a warning and returns void. The queue that drives it declares `attempts: 3`. Because the service can never throw, the job always completes successfully, so the three attempts are unreachable: a fault after page 1 leaves a brand permanently holding a partial branch set, the job is marked done, and nothing anywhere records that the set is partial. The failure and the success are the same observable. | LADDER: the catch compensates for the correct instinct that one brand's expansion must not kill the pass. Bedrock: not crashing and not telling anyone are different decisions, and only the first was made (the identical shape F205 names for the signals crons). Worse here, because the caller is a QUEUE that already implements the right behaviour — retry — and is prevented from using it. Rederive: let the loop throw; the queue's `attempts: 3` then means what it says, and per-page progress is already idempotent (upsert keyed on googlePlaceId, `seenPlaceIds` rebuilt from stored locations each run) so a retry resumes rather than repeats. If a swallow must remain, it must be visible in a RETURN value (`{complete: boolean}`) that the caller records — which is the same fact F353 needs for the metro test. Red team: throwing makes a vendor outage retry three times at Places cost instead of zero — that is the trade, and it is the one the queue's author already chose for the primary lane; the alternative (silent permanent truncation) is worse because it corrupts the location set that P2.2 will reason over. | FIXED (owner-ruled 2026-08-03, D32 escalation: YES to throwing) | PROOF: read; the catch at :2442 had no rethrow; queue `attempts: 3` at :49. || PASS-3 PROOF: the catch is GONE — `enrichSecondaryLocations` throws, the worker does not swallow, and the queue's attempts:3 is reachable for the first time. THE IDEMPOTENCE CLAIM WAS VERIFIED, NOT ASSUMED, and it was HALF FALSE: upserts keyed on the unique `googlePlaceId` and a `seenPlaceIds` rebuilt each attempt from a freshly re-read `include: { locations: true }` are real (single caller, restaurant-location-enrichment.service.ts:520-579), BUT the loop's `processedThisPage === 0` break meant a retry — whose page 1 is entirely already-stored — STOPPED AT PAGE 1 and never reached the page that faulted. The resume was a resume in name only. The break test now counts qualifying branches PRESENT on the page (`processedThisPage + alreadyStoredThisPage`), not rows WRITTEN, excluding the canonical place so a zero-branch brand still stops after page 1 and buys no second page. Two consequential side-effects, both named in code: `removeOnFail` 50->true (a retained failed job squats on the jobId and silently no-ops the next enqueue — harmless while nothing could fail, harmful the moment failure is real) and the primary lane's exponential backoff mirrored (three attempts back-to-back would triple a vendor blip's Places bill in seconds). Spend authority unchanged: same per-op ceilings, same 60-result cap. SPEC restaurant-secondary-location-expansion.spec.ts, 9 cases, 4 RED-proved by mutation: reinstating the worker's swallow, reverting the pagination-resume test, dropping the queue's campaign capture, and dropping the worker's runInWorkContext each fail exactly one case.

F355 | api-places-enrichment | restaurant-entity-merge.service.ts:183-219 (mergeLocations) + prisma/schema.prisma:136,154 | TWO SOURCES OF TRUTH FOR "THE PRIMARY LOCATION", AND THE UNCONSTRAINED ONE IS WRONG 398 TIMES. `core_entities.primary_location_id` is a real FK — structurally single. `core_restaurant_locations.is_primary` is a plain Boolean with only a non-unique index. MEASURED on the local mirror: 398 restaurants carry MORE THAN ONE `is_primary = true` row; and yet the FK and the boolean never disagree about WHICH row is primary (0 rows where the FK points at a non-primary, 0 restaurants with locations but no primary flag). So the boolean is not a different answer — it is the same answer plus 398 false extras. F357 | api-places-enrichment | attribute-ontology.service.ts:160-290 + attribute-ontology.worker.ts:43 | THE ADJUDICATION LOOP HAS NO CEILING ON ITS OWN SIZE, AND ITS COST IS LINEAR IN A NUMBER NOBODY CHOSE. `buildPlan` issues one `placeAttribute` LLM call PER CANDIDATE (pass 1, concurrency 12), one more per NEW canonical (pass 2), and one `chooseAttributeName` per new canonical that absorbed synonyms (pass 3) — plus one embedding pass over every candidate AND every active canonical. F358 | api-places-enrichment | estimators/estimator-registry.ts:204-228, 63-65, 23-30, 94 | THE EXPLORATION MECHANISM THE REGISTRY _FORCES_ YOU TO DECLARE IS INVERTED AT THE ONE CASE IT EXISTS FOR — PLUS TWO DECLARED LAWS WITH NO IMPLEMENTATION AND ONE DEAD FIELD. `register()` refuses any self-gating estimator that does not declare an exploration mechanism (a genuinely good structural law). But `read()` computes `uncertainty = sqrt(variance / total)` from OBSERVED variance alone, so a subject with ZERO observations gets variance 0 and therefore uncertainty 0 — maximum confidence from no data. `EstimatorReading.uncertainty`'s own docstring says "Infinity when no data and no prior", and the staged-off branch twenty lines above correctly returns Infinity; the enabled branch returns 0. For `optimisticSelection` — documented as "a starved candidate can always re-demonstrate" — the upper-confidence bound of a never-observed subject is exactly the prior, which is BELOW that of any subject with real variance, so the starved candidate is ranked LAST. The mechanism does the opposite of its stated job. Separately: `versionBindings` is declared by 4 configs and read by NOTHING, and no API exists to change a bound version — so the header's law "a bound version change widens uncertainty / flags re-probe instead of silently mixing regimes" is asserted in prose and implemented nowhere; `hierarchy` is declared with four meanings ("Place-keyed estimators shrink along the places containment DAG") and never read by the registry — the shrinkage lives in PollSupplyEstimators.hierarchicalRead, which takes name+placeId explicitly and ignores `config.hierarchy`, so a second consumer calling plain `read()` on a 'placesDag' estimator silently gets no shrinkage and nothing says so; and `weightSquares` is incremented and decayed on every observation and never read at all. | LADDER: all four compensate for a primitive that was specified more completely than it was built (one commit, "Phase A"), and the type then made the unbuilt parts look built. Rederive: (1) uncertainty must account for the prior's own dispersion so that n=0 yields the WIDEST interval, not the narrowest — the minimal honest form is to floor it by a prior-derived term that decays as nEffective grows, which is the same self-erasure the estimate already implements; (2) either implement version binding (a `bindVersion(name, value)` that widens or resets on change) or DELETE `versionBindings` and the header clause — a law with no enforcement is the always-green disease at the level of documentation; (3) move `hierarchicalRead` INTO the registry keyed off `config.hierarchy`, so declaring 'placesDag' does the thing (the poll module's implementation is the working reference); (4) delete `weightSquares`. Both assertions PASSED. grep confirms zero readers for `versionBindings`, `weightSquares`, and `config.hierarchy`. || PASS-3 PROOF (D31): uncertainty is Infinity whenever dispersion is UNMEASURED — a staged-off reader, or fewer than two effective observations (a spread needs two points; the threshold is definitional, not tuned). A zero-observation subject now carries the widest interval and WINS an optimistic-selection comparison. RED-proved: 3 of the 4 new estimator-registry cases fail against the pre-D31 registry (git stash + rerun). Consumers already guarded for non-finite uncertainty (poll-supply-controller.ts:139, poll-weekly-ritual.service.ts:920); poll-supply + weekly-ritual suites green unchanged. STILL OPEN: versionBindings, config.hierarchy and weightSquares remain declared-and-unread — D31 ruled only on the exploration inversion.

F400 | api-core | apps/api/src/shared/logging/logger.service.ts (whole file) vs logger.interface.ts + winston-logger.service.ts + shared.module.ts:22-25 | **THE API SENDS NO LOGGED ERROR TO SENTRY, AND THE SPEC THAT WOULD CATCH THAT TESTS AN ORPHAN.** There are TWO classes named `LoggerService`. (b) `logging/logger.service.ts` — a `@Injectable()` CONCRETE class carrying `captureToSentry`, whose header states "everything the codebase considers an error-level event ... flows through this one method, so Sentry capture lives here and nowhere else." Nothing imports (b) except its own spec. The DI-wired logger is `WinstonLoggerService`, which extends (a) and has NO Sentry code at all. So every HTTP 500 (GlobalExceptionFilter → `logger.error`), every cron/background catch, and every boot failure is written to stdout and goes NOWHERE else. Only `main.ts`'s process-level `unhandledRejection`/`uncaughtException` handlers and `debug.controller.ts` reach Sentry. Three separate comments assert the working seam and all three are false: `sentry.module.ts:9` ("The one capture seam is LoggerService.error (shared/logging/logger.service.ts)"), `global-exception.filter.ts:196` ("error level IS the Sentry seam — LoggerService.error captures"), and the seam spec's own preamble ("a refactor that severs the seam turns the suite red"). `git log` shows commit 7a2d83877 "crash reporting — one-seam design, both apps" added `captureToSentry` to the orphan — the API seam has never worked. Bedrock: a seam is not a seam because a comment says so; it is a seam because the SHIPPED object goes through it. Consequences that are already live: (1) the Swagger gate's own comment says "Dev/staging only" but staging runs `NODE_ENV=production`, so staging has NO docs — the comment describes the opposite of the code; (2) `getDatabasePoolSize()`'s `case 'staging': return '25'` is UNREACHABLE, because staging is spelled in `APP_ENV`, never `NODE_ENV` (it silently gets prod's 50); (3) `sentry.environment` falls back to `NODE_ENV`, so staging reports as `production` in Sentry unless `SENTRY_ENVIRONMENT` is set by hand — the exact indistinguishability `app-env.ts` was written to end; (4) `cloudinary.envPrefix` defaults to `'dev'`, so a deployed env missing `CLOUDINARY_ENV_PREFIX` writes assets into the dev namespace. | LADDER: NODE_ENV predates `AppEnv` and is load-bearing for tooling (`yarn install --production`, Nest, jest), so it cannot simply be renamed. Every decision about exposure, secrets, sampling and namespaces is the second kind. Rederive: `main.ts` resolves `const appEnv = resolveAppEnv()` once and passes it down; helmet/HSTS/CORS/validation/Swagger key off `isDeployedEnv(appEnv)`; error-detail redaction keys off `isDeployedEnv` too (staging should not leak internals either); `sentry.environment` defaults to `appEnv`; `cloudinary.envPrefix` defaults to `appEnv`; `getDatabasePoolSize` takes `AppEnv` so its staging arm becomes reachable; NODE_ENV survives only where a toolchain reads it. F407 | api-core | apps/api/src/shared/logging/logging.interceptor.ts:150-178 vs src/shared/filters/global-exception.filter.ts:186-222 | **EVERY FAILED REQUEST IS LOGGED TWICE, AND THE INTERCEPTOR'S COPY IGNORES THE BY-STATUS LAW THE FILTER ENFORCES.** `LoggingInterceptor`'s `error` subscriber calls `this.logger.error(...)` for ANY exception, then the same exception reaches `GlobalExceptionFilter`, which logs it again. The filter is deliberate about level — its comment reads "Level by STATUS, never by exception class ... A typed AppException carrying a 500 must not hide at warn" — and correctly downgrades 4xx to `warn`. The interceptor has no status check at all, so a plain 404 or a validation 400 is emitted at ERROR level. Today that only costs duplicate log lines; the moment F400 is repaired it means **every 404 becomes a Sentry event**, which is precisely the metered-quota burn the debug-routes gate (F402) was hardened to prevent. Also note the interceptor reads `response.statusCode` in the error path, which on Fastify is still 200 at that point — the logged `statusCode` on failures is usually wrong. | LADDER: the interceptor's error branch compensates for the filter not existing yet, or for a fear that the filter might not catch everything. Bedrock: there is exactly one place that knows an exception's HTTP status, and it is the exception filter; an interceptor that fires before status resolution cannot classify severity and should not try. Rederive: delete `logError` from the interceptor and its `error` subscriber's logging (keep the `subscriber.error(error)` propagation); the filter remains the sole error logger, already correctly levelled and already carrying correlationId/userId. Red team: the only loss is a log line for an exception that somehow bypasses the global filter — impossible for HTTP, and the filter is `@Catch()` unqualified. **This must land BEFORE or WITH F400**, or repairing crash reporting floods Sentry with 4xx. | FIXED (D33, landed FIRST) — `logError` and the error-subscriber's logging are deleted from `LoggingInterceptor`; `subscriber.error(error)` propagation is unchanged. `GlobalExceptionFilter` is the sole error logger, already levelled by STATUS and already carrying correlationId + the VERIFIED userId. The interceptor now carries the reason, including why it cannot classify severity (on Fastify `response.statusCode` is still 200 in the error path). | **PROOF (executed, mutation-proven):** new `logging.interceptor.spec.ts` — a thrown exception is logged at NO level (neither error nor warn), the exception still propagates unchanged, and successful responses still log at http. RED PROOF: re-adding a `this.logger.error(...)` to the error subscriber turns it RED ('Expected number of calls: 0, Received number of calls: 1'). Restored → green.

F408 | api-core | apps/api/src/shared/logging/correlation.utils.ts:113-141, used at logging.interceptor.ts:38-44 | **THE `userId` IN EVERY REQUEST LOG IS ATTACKER-CONTROLLED.** `extractUserIdFromToken` base64-decodes the JWT payload segment and returns `sub`/`userId` **with no signature verification** — its own comment says "In production, you'd use proper JWT verification". Bedrock: an unverified claim is not an identity; the correct value for "who is this" before authentication runs is _unknown_. Rederive: delete `extractUserIdFromToken` (69 lines incl. its `manual base64` path) and leave `context.userId` undefined at request-log time; populate it from `request.user.userId` in the RESPONSE log and in the filter's `logContext` (the filter already reads `request.user.userId` at :204 — the verified one). Correlation across the request is already carried by `correlationId`, which is what it is for. Red team: incoming request lines lose a userId they were never entitled to assert; every line that matters (response, error) gains a verified one. | ESCALATED (design proposal; security-relevant) | read; `correlation.utils.ts:127` `Buffer.from(token.split('.')[1],'base64')` with no verify step, called unconditionally at `logging.interceptor.ts:38`.

F414 | api-scripts | apps/api/scripts/ (100 files) | **THE SCRIPTS DIRECTORY HAS NO LIFECYCLE — AND THAT, NOT ROT, IS THE DEFECT.** Full census: `tsc --noEmit` compiles all of it clean, and spot-executed orphans still work (see proof), so nothing here is broken. What is missing is any rule for entry or exit. No `.github/workflows/` file references any script in this directory. Two READMEs (`scripts/data-fixes/README.md`, `scripts/search-harness/README.md`) are linked from nothing. `scripts/lib/gazetteer-names.ts` has no importer at all — its banking note points at `seed-us-places`, a script that no longer exists. | LADDER: compensates for a genuinely useful practice — writing a probe to answer one question during an investigation — colliding with the absence of any convention for what happens to the probe afterward. Bedrock: a script is one of exactly three things and should say which in its own header — (a) **operational tooling** invoked by a runner (package.json / rig / skill), (b) **a banked probe** whose value is the recorded RESULT, kept so the finding is reproducible, or (c) **scratch**, valuable for a day. Rederive: adopt the `rt-*` prefix convention the tsconfig already half-encodes, generalized: a mandatory one-line header on every script naming its class and its runner or its banked finding; `scripts/scratch/` (gitignored) for class (c); a lockdown spec that fails on a script with no class header. NOT DONE (still open, out of ratified scope): the two safe stand-alone deletions the finding names (`scripts/lib/gazetteer-names.ts`, zero importers with its stated consumer deleted) and linking the two orphan READMEs.

Rederive: (a) match keys case-insensitively on a SUBSTRING set (`key`, `token`, `secret`, `password`, `auth`, `cookie`, `session`) so `apiKey`/`accessToken` are caught, and recurse in `sanitizeBody` as `sanitizeNestedObject` already does; (b) better, stop logging request bodies by default — gate it behind a dev-only flag, since the correlationId + route + status already answer every question the body was there for. F422 | api-core | apps/api/src/shared/exceptions/app-exception.base.ts:9,23-28 + all 22 subclasses | **`isOperational` IS A DISCRIMINATOR THAT NEVER DISCRIMINATES — AND ITS ONE EFFECT IS LEAKING INTERNALS TO PROD CLIENTS.** `AppException` declares `abstract readonly isOperational: boolean`, and `getClientSafeMessage(isProd)` redacts the message only when `isProd && !this.isOperational`. A census of every subclass in `apps/api/src` finds **22 declarations, all `= true`, and zero `false`** — including `DatabaseException` (HTTP 500, message `Database create failed for User`), `ExternalServiceException` (502, `Gemini service error during generateContent`), and `DatabaseConfigurationError`. So the redaction branch is unreachable, and `GlobalExceptionFilter:75` returns those messages verbatim to production callers, while the very next branch of the same method carefully replaces a plain `Error` with `'An internal error occurred'`. A typed exception is currently LESS redacted than an untyped one. | LADDER: compensates for wanting to distinguish "an expected failure the client should hear about" from "a bug", encoded as a per-class boolean the author must remember to set correctly — and every author defaulted to `true` because `true` is the permissive, working-looking value. Bedrock: whether a message is safe to show a client is a property of the MESSAGE, not of the class; and the fact the filter actually needs — "is this a 5xx" — is already carried by the status, which is why `logError` was rewritten to level "by STATUS, never by exception class". Rederive: delete `isOperational` and make `getClientSafeMessage(isProd)` redact on `isProd && this.getStatus() >= 500`, matching the untyped path exactly. Exceptions that genuinely want a client-visible 5xx message (none today) would opt in explicitly with a `clientMessage` field, which is a positive assertion rather than a forgotten negative. Red team: prod stops returning DB/vendor internals — the intended behaviour all along; nothing else reads the flag except `getLogContext()`, where it is a constant. | FIXED (D33) — `isOperational` DELETED: the abstract declaration, all 22 `= true` subclass declarations, and the `getLogContext()` field where it was a constant. `getClientSafeMessage(isProd)` now redacts on `isProd && this.getStatus() >= 500`, matching the untyped-error path in the same filter exactly, and matching `logError`'s ratified 'by STATUS, never by exception class'. | **PROOF (executed, mutation-proven):** `client-safe-message.spec.ts` — the Database 5xx message no longer leaks (`'An internal error occurred'`, asserted NOT to contain 'Database'), 4xx still shows, non-prod still shows, the flag cannot return as a per-class opt-out, and a WHOLE-MODULE sweep over every AppException subclass asserts every constructible 5xx redacts (with a non-empty-sweep guard, since an empty loop is a green metric that cannot show red). RED PROOF: neutering the redaction branch turns 2 of the 5 RED, including the whole-module sweep. Census re-verified before deletion: 22 `= true`, zero `false`.

F423 | api-core | apps/api/src/shared/types/error-interfaces.ts:83-90, used at src/shared/filters/global-exception.filter.ts:110-112 | **THE TYPE GUARDS CANNOT SAY NO, AND ONE OF THEM MISCLASSIFIES NETWORK FAILURES AS DATABASE ERRORS IN EVERY HTTP RESPONSE.** `isPrismaError(error)` returns true for anything that is an object with a `code` and a `message` — which describes essentially every Node system error (`ECONNREFUSED`, `ENOTFOUND`, `ETIMEDOUT`), every Axios error, and most vendor SDK errors. `GlobalExceptionFilter.extractErrorDetails` tests it BEFORE the generic branch, so a Redis outage or a Gemini connection reset is reported to the caller as `errorCode: 'DATABASE_ERROR'`, message `'Database operation failed'`, and logged the same way — sending the on-call reader to the wrong subsystem. `isRedditApiError` is worse still (`'error' in error || 'message' in error` — true for every `Error`), and `isHttpError` claims any object with a message and a status. The file's own header calls itself a "Template for gradual migration ... Priority: Medium", yet it sits on the hot path of the global exception filter. | LADDER: compensates for `unknown`-typed catch blocks at a time when the alternative was `any`. Bedrock: a type guard's value is entirely in its ability to return FALSE; a structural test over two ubiquitous field names is not a discriminator, it is an assertion dressed as a check. Prisma ships the real answer — `error instanceof Prisma.PrismaClientKnownRequestError` (and `...UnknownRequestError`, `...ValidationError`), which is exact and already imported elsewhere in this codebase. Rederive: `isPrismaError` becomes the `instanceof` test; `isRedditApiError`/`isLLMApiError`/`isDatabaseConnectionError` are deleted unless a caller can state a field combination unique to that vendor (none currently can); `getErrorMessage`/`getErrorCode` stay — they are honest best-effort extractors and are the only parts with real callers. Red team: `instanceof` fails across duplicate `@prisma/client` copies in a monorepo — verify with a single boot probe, and fall back to `error.name.startsWith('PrismaClient')` if it does; either is vastly narrower than "has a code". The behaviour change is that non-Prisma failures stop being labelled DATABASE_ERROR, which is the whole point. | ESCALATED (design proposal) | read; `filters/global-exception.filter.ts:110` calls `isPrismaError(exception)` ahead of the unexpected-error branch, and `handlePrismaError`'s `default:` arm produces `DATABASE_ERROR` for any unrecognised `code`.

F479 | public-crave-score.service.ts writeScores | THE SCALE NOTE WAS RIGHT, AND THE CEILING IS HEAP, NOT SECONDS. rebuildAllScores scores the WHOLE graph in one run, so `scored.length` IS the corpus (24,032 subjects on the mirror), and the write built one `$executeRaw` per subject and handed the whole array to `$transaction`. MEASURED on the mirror against a clone of the real table: 24,032 subjects = 2,229 ms per-row vs 643 ms set-based; at 10x (240,320 subjects) = 18,610 ms / **2,461 MB heap** vs 5,251 ms / 790 MB. 2.4 GB of retained statement objects inside one transaction is an OOM on any container we run, reached by corpus growth alone — this is a real ceiling, not a micro-optimisation. | REDERIVED (2026-08-03): ONE `INSERT … SELECT … FROM unnest(...)` upsert; columns travel as parallel arrays. Numerics are bound as **text** and cast `::numeric` deliberately — the columns are `numeric(p,s)` and binding a float64 would re-round on top of the rounding scoreCandidates already did; `String(n)` is the shortest round-trip decimal and `::numeric` parses it exactly. The stale-subject prune stays a second statement in the SAME `$transaction`, so atomicity is unchanged. A NEW PRECONDITION IS NAMED, NOT ASSUMED: the per-row loop silently let a duplicated subject overwrite itself, whereas a set-based upsert raises Postgres' opaque "ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE command cannot affect row a second time" — distinctness is structural (loadCandidates builds both lists by iterating Maps keyed by connectionId/restaurantId, subjectType separating them), so a duplicate means that construction broke upstream, and writeScores now refuses by name. | FIXED | PROOF: (a) EQUIVALENCE, byte-level — both shapes fed the identical 24,032 live subjects into two clones of the real table; symmetric difference across all 11 written columns = **0 rows**. (b) public-crave-score.write-shape.spec.ts, 9 specs (single statement for 500 subjects; 8 parallel arrays each of batch length; text-bound numerics; null `rising` stays a null element not the string "null"; prune atomic and ordered; fixture run emits no prune; duplicate refused by name; same id under a different subject_type is NOT a duplicate; empty run writes nothing). (c) RED PROOF EXECUTED: reverted both source files to HEAD, the two new suites went 14 failed / 5 passed, then restored. (d) LIVE: the real `scripts/rebuild-crave-scores.ts` against the mirror — 24,015 subjects, 3,162 ms, one score_run_id in the table (prune correct), rising populated, display 0.00–10.00, zero empty factor traces.

F480 | projection-rebuild.service.ts loadActiveRestaurantEvents / loadActiveRestaurantEntityEvents | ACTIVE-RUN WAS A POST-FILTER FOR A PREDICATE THE DB OWNS — AND THE DISCARD GROWS WITHOUT BOUND. Both loaders fetched every generation's events for the batch, carried `sourceDocument.activeExtractionRunId` through the ORM solely to compare it in JS, and dropped the losers. Prisma cannot express it (a column-to-column comparison across a relation), which is WHY it drifted to JS — but the same file already states the predicate in raw SQL twice, in sweepTombstoneEvents' repoint and dup-delete CTEs, so this was the odd dialect out of three. THE GROWTH IS DESIGNED, NOT HYPOTHETICAL: `supersedeAndActivate` only DELETES a superseded generation sharing the activating run's `systemPromptHash`, so a re-extraction under an ITERATED prompt — the entire point of the re-extract rail — retains its predecessor permanently; rows fetched grow one full generation per prompt version while rows kept stay at one. | REDERIVED (2026-08-03): both loaders are `$queryRaw` with `JOIN collection_source_documents sd ON sd.document_id = ev.source_document_id AND sd.active_extraction_run_id = ev.extraction_run_id`, which is the only form that both excludes before the wire and can use `idx_source_documents_active_run`. The `sourceDocument` member on `ActiveRestaurantEvent`/`ActiveRestaurantEntityEvent` — which existed ONLY to be filtered on, zero other consumers, re-grepped — is deleted from both types. Empty batch short-circuits rather than emitting `ANY('{}')`. | FIXED | PROOF: measured on the mirror, hottest 50-restaurant batch = 12,271 rows, **121 ms findMany+JS filter vs 59 ms joined**; today's corpus holds exactly one generation so the JS filter discarded 0 (verified: 90,250 of 90,250 entity events and 28,320 of 28,320 restaurant events are active) — the win is the growth curve, and that is stated rather than dressed up as a present-day 2x. projection-rebuild.active-run.spec.ts, 10 specs across both loaders, asserting on the REAL emitted SQL: the join predicate is present; the ORM loaders are NOT called; `sd.active_extraction_run_id` appears exactly once (join, never SELECT); the batch binds as one array param; an empty batch queries nothing. F481 | archive-ingestion.service.ts:546 `postsById` | SCALE NOTE PREMISE CORRECTED. The note read "archive loads whole corpus into a Map" against a multi-GB run — but the multi-GB thing is the COMPRESSED FILE, which is streamed and never materialised; the Map holds only the stage-0 survivors (3-year window + structural drops applied BEFORE `set`). The Map is also not incidental: submissions and comments arrive in TWO SEPARATE archive files, so it IS the join, and it is bounded per subreddit because `loadArchivePosts` runs one subreddit at a time. | **ARGUED-IDEAL — not churned.** MEASURED heap for the real corpus shape (r/austinfood: 1,328 posts / 37,799 comments, avg 350 and 125 chars): **8 MB**. At 10x: 73 MB. At 50x (66k posts / 1.86M comments — bigger than any sub we would onboard): 328 MB. The mandate's own restraint clause applies: fine at 10x, recorded with numbers instead of rewritten. The ceiling, if it is ever wanted, is the largest single subreddit's in-window content, and the lever that bounds it (PUSHSHIFT_WINDOW_YEARS=3) is already ratified in F470.

F482 | food-dedupe-merge.service.ts refreshSortedIdentityKeys | SCALE NOTE PREMISE FALSE, AND THE SHAPE IS LOAD-BEARING. The note read "17k sequential heal UPDATEs", but 17,357 is the SELECT's row count, not the UPDATE count — the loop writes only rows whose recomputed key DRIFTED. MEASURED by running the real `canonicalFold`/`entityIdentityKey` over all 17,357 live rows: **0 drifted**. Steady state is one 51 ms SELECT and zero writes. Worst case is a fold-version change (every row drifts), measured end-to-end at **1,728 ms** for all 17,357 sequential UPDATEs — a one-off, on a nightly maintenance sweep. | **ARGUED-IDEAL — and batching it would be a REGRESSION.** The per-row shape is required by the convergent-sweep law the code already documents (round-12 F2): each UPDATE is individually wrapped so a 23505 collision logs one merge candidate and the sweep KEEPS GOING. A set-based UPDATE would abort the whole statement on the first collision — precisely the all-or-nothing failure that law exists to prevent. The loop is slow-looking on purpose; leave it.

### the api seam

F803 | mobile-app-core | eas.json:10 vs src/services/api.ts:11,242 | **EVERY EAS BUILD POINTS AT THE WRONG BASE URL.** `build.base.env.EXPO_PUBLIC_API_URL = "https://api-production-a56f.up.railway.app"` — no `/api/v1`. So a development/preview/production EAS build calls `https://…/search`, `https://…/users/me` and 404s on everything. It has not bitten because the day-to-day sim reads `.env.local`, which carries the suffix. The base-URL truth lives in four places (eas.json, .env.example, .env.local, the DEFAULT_API_URL constant) and three of them agree. | one place: put the `/api/v1` suffix INSIDE the client (`baseURL = ${origin}/api/v1`) and let the env carry only an origin; then a missing suffix is impossible | FIXED (D38) — eas.json's `build.base.env.EXPO_PUBLIC_API_URL` now carries the `/api/v1` global prefix, so every EAS profile (development/development-device/preview/production) calls a real base instead of 404ing on the origin. The agreement between the four homes of that URL is now ASSERTED, not trusted: services/api-base-url.spec.ts checks every EXPO_PUBLIC_API_URL in eas.json, the .env.example template, and the client's DEFAULT_API_URL fallback. F804 | mobile-app-core | src/services/api.ts:304-383 | **THE ONE CLIENT HAS NO 401 SEAM.** The response interceptor handles 403+ENTITLEMENT_REQUIRED and >=500, and nothing else. A 401 (expired/revoked Clerk session, or `getAuthToken` returning null because the token resolver threw — :265-271 swallows that into `logger.warn` + null) falls through to the generic failure modal, and the app keeps making unauthenticated requests forever with no sign-out and no re-auth prompt. The AuthProvider's resolver is the only refresh path and it has no retry. LADDER — compensates-for: nothing; the case was simply never written. bedrock: Clerk owns refresh, but the CLIENT owns "the refresh failed, now what". rederive: one `on401` branch beside the 403 branch — clear the query cache, announce through a session-lapse store the way `entitlementLapseStore` does for entitlement, and let the route coordinator show sign-in. red-team: "Clerk auto-refreshes so 401 can't happen" — it can (revoked session, deleted user, clock skew, the resolver's own catch), and today the failure mode is an app that silently degrades to anonymous. | FIXED (D38) — ONE explicit 401 seam. `resolveApiFailureAction` (services/api-failure-policy.ts) closes the outcome set — session_lapse / entitlement_lapse / service_issue / caller_owned — and the response interceptor now dispatches on it instead of testing two ad-hoc conditions and letting 401 fall through. A 401 announces through `useSessionLapseStore` (mirroring entitlementLapseStore), tags the error `isSessionLapse`, and AppRouteCoordinator makes the SERVER's verdict win over Clerk's cached `isSignedIn`: authStatus becomes 'signed_out', the react-query cache is cleared, and the route is sign-in. Silent-anonymous is no longer representable. The lapse clears on a real session change (signed out, or a new user id). MUTATION-PROVED: api-failure-policy.spec.ts, 8 pass, incl. 'THE TRANSITION: a 401 flips the app into an explicit signed-out state'; deleting the `status === 401` case fails 2 cases including the store transition | read the whole interceptor + AuthProvider token resolver

### errors that reach nobody

F810 | mobile-app-core | src/screens/Onboarding.tsx:451-463 | **SILENT LOSS OF THE ONE THING ONBOARDING EXISTS TO COLLECT.** When the user is signed in and `usersService.completeOnboarding` throws, the catch logs a warn, CLEARS the service-issue banner (`clearServiceIssue('global')` — actively hiding the evidence), and marks onboarding complete LOCALLY. The persisted status is now `completed`, so the flow never runs again and the payload — every answer, plus the username claim — is never retried or replayed. The user believes they finished; the server has nothing. There is no outbox and no reconciliation on next launch. LADDER — compensates-for: a real fear, that a network blip strands a user on the last onboarding screen. bedrock: the answers are the product's cold-start signal; losing them silently is worse than a retry. rederive: complete locally AND enqueue the payload for replay (the answers already live in the persisted zustand draft — keep the draft until the server confirms, and re-send on next authenticated launch). What becomes impossible: a completed-locally user whose answers never landed. | keep the draft until server-confirmed; replay on launch | FIXED (D38) — the answers are DURABLE DATA (owner, 2026-08-03) and can no longer be discarded. The catch no longer clears the service-issue banner and no longer marks onboarding complete: it records the exact rejected payload in a PERSISTED outbox (`onboardingStore.pendingServerCompletion`, in `partialize` so it survives a cold start), surfaces the failure through `completionError` (the CTA stays live, so pressing it again retries), and returns false. AppRouteCoordinator replays the payload on the next authenticated launch via `decideOnboardingCompletionReplay`; only a CONFIRMED server write empties the outbox, and it NEVER expires — a payload we cannot land today is still the only copy of the user's answers.
