RE-DERIVED onto today's tree where it was not: (1) the DTO no longer accepts client `successUrl`/`cancelUrl` — an open redirect wearing a feature's clothes; all three redirect URLs plus the price id come from config with NO defaults (no-fake-estimates: a guessed price sells the wrong thing, a guessed redirect strands a payer), and an unconfigured rail 503s naming the missing env vars. (2) SINGLE-PRODUCT LAW is now enforced on BOTH doors: a `priceId` that is not the configured premium price is a 400 naming both ids, and a subscription arriving with an `entitlement_code` outside the closed ledger vocabulary throws (event recorded FAILED + replayable) instead of minting a paid grant under a code `accessVerdict()` never asks about — the same D1-residual hole `RevenueCatEntitlementMap` refuses at boot, closed on the Stripe side. (3) ENTITLEMENTS UNIFY THROUGH THE ACCESS-GRANT LEDGER, not the restored table: `checkout.session.completed` retrieves the subscription and funnels into the same `syncSubscriptionGrant` the subscription events use, idempotent per `stripe:<subId>`, so whichever of the two events Stripe delivers first is sufficient and the second is a no-op. The table is the ATTEMPT log only. (4) `subscription_data.metadata` is stamped at session creation — Stripe does NOT copy Checkout Session metadata onto the subscription, so without it every web subscription event would log "without matching user" and grant nothing. (5) `ensureStripeCustomer` came back into BillingService rather than UserService: it is billing's business and nothing else ever called it. (6) The recreated table is timestamptz throughout and FK RESTRICT, per the laws that postdate its deletion. | FIXED (2026-08-03) | PROOF: `npx jest billing entitlements` 86/86 green (12 new in billing-checkout.spec.ts, stripe SDK mocked — zero live vendor calls); `yarn build` clean; migration applied locally and `prisma migrate diff` shows ZERO checkout drift. **AMENDED 2026-08-03 (same day, owner ruling): TWO PRICES OF THE ONE PRODUCT, and the single-product law got STRONGER, not looser.** The owner ruled that the web paywall shows the SAME structure as the in-app one (Strava pattern: same offers, different payment location) — $7.99/mo and $39.99/yr with an annual-only ~1-week free trial. So `stripe.premiumPriceId` (STRIPE_PREMIUM_PRICE_ID) became the closed pair `stripe.prices.{monthly,annual}` (STRIPE_MONTHLY_PRICE_ID / STRIPE_ANNUAL_PRICE_ID), and the DTO's `priceId` field was DELETED in favour of `{ plan: 'monthly' | 'annual' }`. Note what this does to the law: the original shape enforced 'premium is the only product' by comparing a client-supplied opaque Stripe id against the configured one — a refusal. A two-word vocabulary makes a price id outside the configured pair UNREPRESENTABLE, because the caller cannot name a price at all; the api alone maps word -> price. One PRODUCT, two PRICES of it; `entitlement_code` metadata is identical on both plans, so both grant the same thing `accessVerdict()` asks about. `plan` is REQUIRED, never defaulted — a paywall showing two prices against a body that silently means 'monthly' is a charge the user did not pick. The trial lives in the SESSION (`subscription_data.trial_period_days = ANNUAL_TRIAL_PERIOD_DAYS = 7`, annual only, spread in rather than set-to-undefined) not on the Stripe price, so the offer the copy promises and the offer the code builds are the same object. `requireCheckoutConfig()` requires BOTH prices regardless of the requested plan: a half-configured rail must 503 on the FIRST request, not on the unlucky user who picks the other button. PROOF: `npx jest billing --silent` 53/53 green; `yarn build` clean; zero live vendor calls (stripe SDK still mocked wholesale). ORIGINAL-PASS PROOF: replacing the single-product price check with `if (false)` and the replayed-event short-circuit with `if (false)` turns exactly 2 tests red ("REFUSES a second product", "idempotent on REPLAY — zero extra grants"); restored, 12/12 green. NOT DONE (out of scope, reported): no Stripe key was used, nothing deployed, mobile client not wired.

F1000 | mobile-search | runtime/scheduler/runtime-work-scheduler.ts:148-153 + frame-budget-governor.ts:17-22 | THE ANTI-STARVATION MECHANISM IS STRUCTURALLY DEAD. `canStarvationOverride` = `starvationOverrideEligible && !isCriticalPressure() && !STARVATION_OVERRIDE_DISABLED_LANES.has(lane)`. `starvationOverrideEligible` can only become true for a lane with a FINITE `MAX_DEFERRED_FRAMES_BY_LANE` entry — and that map has exactly three keys {selection*feedback, phase_b_materialization, overlay_shell_transition}, ALL THREE of which are members of STARVATION_OVERRIDE_DISABLED_LANES. Every other lane gets POSITIVE_INFINITY and is never eligible. Therefore `canStarvationOverride` is a compile-time-constant FALSE, and the `deferredFrameCount` bookkeeping (L157) feeds nothing. A guard that cannot fail. Failure enabled: a deferred phase_b/overlay task can be starved indefinitely under sustained frame pressure with no escape hatch, while the code reads as though one exists. Ladder: compensates-for = wanting both "heavy lanes must not hog a frame" and "heavy lanes must not starve"; bedrock = those are the SAME set of lanes, so the two policies were written against each other; rederive = pick one owner for heavy-lane admission — either the governor's one-heavy-lane-per-frame rule (which already bounds hogging) OR a deferral cap, not both, and make the cap apply to the lanes it was written for; red-team = the dead override may be load-bearing-by-absence (enabling it could admit a heavy task during critical pressure and regress the very jank the governor was built to kill), so this must be re-derived as a decision, not "fixed" by deleting a set membership. | FIXED (Phase 3, 2026-08-03) | The override DIED rather than being switched on: MAX_DEFERRED_FRAMES_BY_LANE, STARVATION_OVERRIDE_DISABLED_LANES (the byte-identical HEAVY_LANES duplicate), canStarvationOverride and the deferredFrameCount field+bookkeeping are all deleted. ONE OWNER for heavy-lane admission — the governor one-heavy-lane-per-frame rule. Enabling the override would have been an unmeasured behavior change under exactly the pressure the governor exists to relieve (no-fake-estimates law), so the honest move was deletion plus a comment naming the fairness that actually exists: head-retention (a deferred task is unshifted and the frame ENDS). PROOF: runtime-work-scheduler.spec.ts, new; RED PROVEN by changing the unshift to push (1 failure)

Any value reaching L64 is already <= 12, hence always <= 12.67 — L64 is tautologically TRUE. Ladder: compensates-for = two budget models (a frame-headroom model and a hard/soft-budget model) landed on top of each other; bedrock = there is ONE budget question ("may this task run in the remaining frame?"); rederive = delete the headroom model and keep hard/soft, or derive HARD_BUDGET_MS FROM `TARGET_FRAME_MS - RESERVED_HEADROOM_MS` so the constants are related by construction instead of by coincidence; red-team = the 12 vs 12.67 gap is only 0.67ms, so behavior is unchanged either way — this is a legibility/honesty fix, not a perf fix, and should not be sold as one. | FIXED (Phase 3, 2026-08-03) | TARGET_FRAME_MS, RESERVED_HEADROOM_MS, availableBudgetMs and the tautological final return are deleted; canRun is now one budget model (hard 12 / soft 8, first-task exemption). isCriticalPressure() went with the override that was its only caller. F963 | mobile-nav-overlays | apps/mobile/src/overlays/edit-mode-session-core.ts:18 | CORRECTNESS BY UNSTATED COINCIDENCE. `return baseline == null || baseline.join(' ') !== live.order.join(' ');` compares two string-id arrays by joining them with a space. F1037 | mobile-search | runtime/shared/search-open-now-projection.ts | IDEAL-VERIFIED on the single most-suspected client-re-derivation in the territory — and the suspicion was WRONG, recorded so the next pass does not re-hunt it. "Open now" is NOT recomputed client-side: the projection FILTERS on the server-provided `operatingStatus.isOpen` (rows) and the API's per-feature `isOpen` (coverage). It never parses an hours string and never consults the device clock. Three things make it exemplary: (1) rows WITHOUT openness data are DROPPED, explicitly "matching the server's open-now post-filter semantics exactly" — the client mirrors server semantics rather than inventing gentler ones; (2) `coverageCarriesOpenness` is a real VERSION-SKEW guard that can fail — an older API omitting `isOpen` would silently empty the coverage, so the projection DECLINES instead of producing a confidently-wrong empty map; (3) the projected totals are marked PROVISIONAL in the metadata and the resolver settles them with the honest server slice as a version update (no second reveal), so the optimistic paint can never harden into a wrong number. This is the correct shape for optimistic client projection of a server truth, and it is the counter-example that isolates F1018/F1019: the re-derivation disease in this territory is NOT in the runtime layer, it is confined to the components/utils layer. | IDEAL-VERIFIED | full read + compared against the server's open-now post-filter

F1101 | mobile-native | apps/mobile/ios/cravesearch/cravesearch.entitlements:1-8 (whole file) + apps/mobile/src/providers/AuthProvider.tsx:226 | THE ENTITLEMENTS FILE HARDCODES `aps-environment = development` AND NOTHING ELSE, while the app really does register for push: `Notifications.getExpoPushTokenAsync({ projectId })` runs in AuthProvider, and `src/services/push-permission.ts:79` requests the OS permission. `aps-environment` selects WHICH APNs the token is minted against — `development` = the sandbox gateway. Failure scenario: a TestFlight/App Store build carrying this value mints sandbox tokens; the api pushes to production APNs; every notification silently disappears with no client-visible error (BadDeviceToken server-side at most). This is the classic "push works on my sim, dies in TestFlight" bug, and it is invisible until real users are on the build. Caveat kept honest: EAS's managed-credential flow can rewrite the entitlement at archive time from the provisioning profile, so this MAY be masked in practice — but the repo cannot prove that, and `eas.json` has no ios credentials block. Ladder: the value is the Expo prebuild default for a dev-only app; it compensated for "we only ever ran a dev client". Bedrock = the entitlement is `$(APS_ENVIRONMENT)` driven per-configuration (development for Debug, production for Release), so the shipped value is a consequence of the build, not a constant. | **RESOLVED-AS-NON-DEFECT (2026-08-03), + instrument added.** MECHANISM (proved from installed source, not plausibility): the APNs environment is chosen from the EMBEDDED PROVISIONING PROFILE at runtime, never from this file. `node_modules/expo-notifications/build/getExpoPushTokenAsync.js:60` sets the request's `development` flag from `shouldUseDevelopmentNotificationService()` (:150-160), which calls `Application.getIosPushNotificationServiceEnvironmentAsync()`; that resolves in `node_modules/expo-application/ios/EXApplication/EXProvisioningProfile.m:28-36` by reading `Entitlements["aps-environment"]` out of the bundle's `embedded.mobileprovision`. Expo's push service therefore routes each token to sandbox/production by what the SIGNED PROFILE says. A store profile (eas.json `production`: `"distribution": "store"`, no `credentialsSource` ⇒ EAS remote managed credentials mint an App Store distribution profile) and an ad-hoc profile both carry `production`; only development-signed builds carry `development`. Xcode's packaging step independently substitutes the profile's aps-environment into the signed `.xcent`, so the compiled literal here is not what ships either. `app.json:43-45` mirrors the same dev value and is equally inert (the ios/ project is authoritative and is not prebuilt). NO CODE FIX NEEDED — the entitlements comment now states why `development` is correct. INSTRUMENT (so the next TestFlight build proves itself): `reportPushEnvironmentClassification()` in `apps/mobile/src/providers/AuthProvider.tsx` runs before every `getExpoPushTokenAsync`, logs `[PushEnv] apsEnvironment=… releaseType=…`, and fires `captureHandledError` (Sentry, seam `push:aps-environment`) ONLY on the genuinely broken combination — a distributed build (APP_STORE/TestFlight, AD_HOC, ENTERPRISE) reporting a non-production APNs environment. It can show RED. `expo-application` promoted from transitive to a direct dep (`~7.0.8`, already pod-linked via expo-notifications). Verified: plutil -lint OK, eas.json parses, tsc error count unchanged (2 pre-existing rnmapbox-typing errors), jest 600/600 green. | plutil -p of the entitlements + grep of getExpoPushTokenAsync/requestPermissionsAsync in src/ + read of getExpoPushTokenAsync.js + EXProvisioningProfile.m + eas.json profiles

F1106 | mobile-native | apps/mobile/ios/cravesearch/Info.plist (3 location keys) vs apps/mobile/src | OVER-DECLARED LOCATION PERMISSIONS. Info.plist declares all three of `NSLocationWhenInUseUsageDescription`, `NSLocationAlwaysUsageDescription` and `NSLocationAlwaysAndWhenInUseUsageDescription`, all with the same generic string "Allow $(PRODUCT_NAME) to access your location". But the app never asks for Always/background: repo-wide grep of `src/` for `requestBackgroundPermissionsAsync` and `startLocationUpdatesAsync` returns ZERO, there is no `UIBackgroundModes` key, and no location background entitlement. F1107 | mobile-native | apps/mobile/ios/cravesearch/Info.plist (no NSPhotoLibrary\* key) vs apps/mobile/src/overlays/PostPhotosFunnelHost.tsx:119 | NO `NSPhotoLibraryUsageDescription` / `NSPhotoLibraryAddUsageDescription` ANYWHERE, while `ImagePicker.launchImageLibraryAsync(...)` IS called on the post-photos path. Honest nuance, stated so this is not overclaimed: expo-image-picker 17 goes through `PHPickerViewController` by default, which is out-of-process and needs NO permission and NO usage string — and the code never calls `requestMediaLibraryPermissionsAsync`, which is consistent with the PHPicker path. So this is very likely NOT a runtime crash today. It IS a live risk on two edges: (a) any option change that drops to the legacy library path, or any future save-to-camera-roll, crashes instantly on a missing usage string — the single most common iOS launch-blocker; (b) Apple's binary analysis flags linked photo-library APIs with no declared purpose. On RN 0.81 with Fabric enabled these run through the interop layers, which WORK (the app ships), so this is not a bug. It is the territory's strategic debt, and it is the honest answer to "what is the ideal shape here": every one of these boundaries is currently untyped (an `NSDictionary` payload on both sides, F1112's signature-drift hazard), synchronous-promise-shaped where a TurboModule could be truly sync, and outside codegen's compile-time contract. It does not always. The reversal branch (:99-109) fires whenever `cardsKey === presentedCardsKey && !identityChanged && !tabChanged`, and the cards key carries BOUNDS (buildSearchCardsWorldKey :326-331, 5-dp lat/lng), so an A→B→A **bounds** reversal (pan, search-this-area, pan back, search-this-area while the first is in flight) reaches it with `prev.filterVariant === next.filterVariant` field-for-field — and is labeled `filter_price`. The kind is the interaction's telemetry identity AND the settleMs-override seam (reconciler :313-314), so the mislabel is not cosmetic: an area reversal is measured, and timed, as a price-chip toggle. Same class one level down: `lens_flip`/`variant_rerun` always DO have a filter delta, so only the reversal arm is wrong. Ladder: compensates for a helper that answers "which chip" when the caller's question is "which interaction"; bedrock = the interaction kind is a fact of the TRANSITION (which the classifier already computed), not something to re-derive from a delta that may be empty. Rederive: the classifier returns the kind alongside the class, or the helper returns `null` and the reversal arm names the honest kind ('retoggle_reversal'/'search_this_area'). F1250 | api-scripts | apps/api/scripts/reload/preserved-anchors.sql:12-50 (the user-anchor set) vs messages.shared_entity_id | **THE USER-ANCHOR LAW HAS A HOLE, AND IT IS THE ONE SURFACE WHOSE WHOLE POINT IS A DURABLE LINK.** wipe-city-derived.sql's law 2 says "any entity a user's data points at ... survives, id intact, so user links can never break", and preserved-anchors.sql enumerates the surfaces: poll targets + topic arrays, list items, photos, curated lists, on-demand requests, signal acts, poll endorsements. It does NOT enumerate `messages.shared_entity_id` — a user sharing a restaurant or dish into a DM (`kind='entity_share'`, `shared_entity_kind` in {restaurant,dish}, the id a bare core_entities uuid resolved through SaveableEntityResolver). The column is `text` with no FK, so nothing else catches it either. Consequence: a wipe deletes an entity a user shared in a conversation, and the share card renders permanently "unavailable" — the exact broken user link the law forbids. The redirect hop cannot rescue it: share-package-resolver.service.ts:150-153 added that hop precisely so a MERGED restaurant stays resolvable, and a wipe DELETES rather than merges, so no redirect row exists. Note the near-miss that makes this a real gap rather than a theoretical one: `user_taste_profile.subject_id` (new 2026-08-03) is also unenumerated but is safe by derivation — it is a projection of `signals`, which IS anchored. Messages are not derived from anything. | LADDER: compensates for the anchor set being an enumeration written when messaging did not exist, in a file whose OWN header calls itself "THE canonical user-anchor set (single source of truth)". An enumeration cannot be a single source of truth for a growing schema — this is the `filesImporting()` disease in SQL. Bedrock: "user data points at this entity" is a property derivable from the SCHEMA (every column, declared-FK or not, that stores a core_entities id and lives in a user-layer table), not from a list someone maintains. Rederive: a spec that reads information_schema, enumerates every uuid/text column in the user layer, and FAILS on any column not either present in preserved-anchors.sql or explicitly listed as derived-and-therefore-covered (with the covering surface named) — so the next `messages` fails a test instead of failing a user. Interim, one-line: add the messages clause. Red team: the text column needs the uuid-shaped filter the poll_endorsements arm already models (kinds list/poll/comment/user_profile are NOT entity ids), so the template exists in the file. | **FIXED (D47, 2026-08-03) — BOTH HALVES.** (a) The `messages` arm is in `preserved-anchors.sql`, kind-filtered to {restaurant,dish} with the uuid-shape guard the poll_endorsements arm modelled. (b) The DEEPER fix landed too: `src/shared/testing/preserved-anchors.spec.ts` derives the census FROM THE SCHEMA — every reference-shaped column in schema.prisma must be either COVERED by an arm (parsed per-arm, FROM-table paired with the columns in that arm, so a name appearing elsewhere in the file cannot fake coverage) or EXEMPT with a written reason naming the anchored surface it derives from. 41 columns classified; the next `messages` fails a test instead of failing a user. | **PROOF (executed, mirror only, ROLLBACK):** built the real scope + `\ir preserved-anchors.sql`, picked a victim entity that is unpreserved AND unreferenced (`red velvet cupcake` 2b23201f-…) so the wipe would delete it, inserted a real `entity_share` message pointing at it, rebuilt the anchor set from scratch → **preserved = f** (RED). The instrument can show both colours, so the RED is the law failing, not the harness lying. **PROOF (executed, D47, mirror only, ROLLBACK):** GREEN — victim food `bihari barbacoa tacos` (unpreserved, unreferenced), real `entity_share` message inserted, anchor set rebuilt from scratch → `preserved = t`, count 5,735 → 5,736 (exactly +1). SPEC mutation: delete the messages arm → the spec fails naming `messages.shared_entity_id` in two tests; restored → 4/4 green. SEAM: `psql crave_search -v communities='austinfood' -v dryrun=1 -f wipe-city-derived.sql` run AFTER the edit → completes with zero errors, every DELETE/UPDATE reports a row count, `DRY RUN — nothing written` + ROLLBACK.

F1252 | api-scripts | apps/api/src/shared/testing/script-containment.spec.ts:44-58, 88-98 vs apps/api/scripts/search-harness/\_shared.ts:70 | **THE CONTAINMENT LOCKDOWN IS OUTFLANKED BY ONE LEVEL OF INDIRECTION — BY THE EXACT DISEASE ITS OWN DOCSTRING CLAIMS TO CURE.** The spec finds scripts by `codeOnly(file).includes('createApplicationContext')`, a FILE-LOCAL string test. 21 search-harness scripts boot the full Nest graph through `bootstrap()` imported from `_shared.ts`; none of them contains the literal, so none is seen. `_shared.ts` itself carries the header, which is why the suite is green. The spec's own comment says "a guard scoped to 'the files I happened to think of' is outflanked by the next file someone adds" — this guard is scoped to the files that happen to spell a particular string, and is outflanked by the next file that calls `bootstrap()`. Two consequences, of unequal size: (a) the CLASS-HEADER assertion misses 21 files — provable, and the direct cause of the 48-row PARTIAL worklist this pass inherited; (b) the CRON assertion misses them too, though the hazard is closed by luck of construction, because `_shared.bootstrap()` happens to call `stopCronsForScript`. (b) is the dangerous half: nothing makes tomorrow's `_shared2.ts` call it. Bedrock: "this script boots Nest" is a property of the module GRAPH, not of one file's text — and the repo already owns the tool, `collectSourceFiles`/`import-scan` is imported at the top of this very spec. Rederive: resolve each script's transitive local imports and treat a script as booting iff ANY file in its closure calls `createApplicationContext`; the class header is then required of the ENTRY POINT (the thing an operator runs), which is the only place it was ever useful. Every level costs a file, an args type, a return type, a dep array that must be kept in sync by hand, and a `ReturnType<typeof …>` import in whoever consumes it. This is the direct cause of several findings above: the dead params of F1317/F1336 survive because no single file sees both the producer and the consumer; the two-name/one-value returns of F1316 are invisible at any one level; F1309's permanently-false gate is only visible if you read four files in order. Per the brief this is RECORDED for the F1012 continuation and explicitly NOT collapsed here — but it is the wave's dominant fact and any rederivation of this territory should start from it rather than from the leaves. red-team = the ceremony is not uniformly worthless: the `*-lane` and `*-authority` boundaries that carry a CONTRACT (`SearchRootStateFoundationLane`, `SearchMapRenderHostAuthority`) buy real decoupling and testability, and F1307's transport machine earns every file it has. The test that separates them is F1012's: does the file own a LIFETIME, a DECISION, or a CONTRACT — or does it only rename fields? | RECORDED for the F1012 continuation (structural; do not collapse piecemeal) | full line-by-line read of all 264 files

### honest coverage split (this territory, after this pass)

Territory totals before: 143 PARTIAL, 21 REDERIVED, 2 DELETED = 166 rows. After: **96 IDEAL-VERIFIED, 50 PARTIAL, 3 DELETED, 17 REDERIVED = 166.**

- **143 PARTIAL rows read line-by-line.** 1 was PHANTOM (F1358) and is now DELETED.
- **96 rows → IDEAL-VERIFIED**, each carrying its OWN one-line argument in COVERAGE (no row was given a generic one): overwhelmingly the pure contract/snapshot modules, the seven identical layout state-controllers, the reducers with spec pins, and the composition roots whose `dispose` tears down in exact reverse construction order.
- **46 of the read rows stay PARTIAL**, each now naming the specific F13xx that keeps it open — a far more useful state than the `F900-F984` cluster reference they all carried before.
- **17 rows keep their pass-1 REDERIVED status UNTOUCHED** because this pass did not read them (`AppRouteCoordinator.tsx`, the `transition-engine/` set incl. the F905/F920 SKIPPED-FOREIGN pair, the policy controllers/registry, `app-route-scene-runtime.ts`, `app-route-sheet-snap-session-runtime.ts`, and three specs). A first cut of this reconciliation swept them into IDEAL-VERIFIED as a side effect of a status rewrite; that would have been the exact dishonesty this pass exists to correct, and they were restored from HEAD.
- **4 rows DOWNGRADED from REDERIVED to PARTIAL** (`app-route-scene-stack-runtime.ts`, `app-route-scene-switch-controller.ts`, `app-route-sheet-host-authority-controller.ts`, `MainLaunchCoordinator.tsx`). These are the jumbos that had only ever been SPOT-read; the full read found F1350/F1351/F1354/F1355/F1356/F1357. Calling them REDERIVED was the pass-1 optimism this pass exists to correct.

### what was NOT found (the new baseline, re-checked not re-litigated)

The transition engine's one-notify-per-operation and supersede-terminates-armed-waits both hold at the one consumer in this territory that depends on them (`app-route-scene-stack-runtime.ts:2077-2116` — F904's fix is correct as written: it watches the txn it ARMED for, so a supersede terminates the wait instead of rearming). `SEEDED_FORWARD_OPEN` and the residency-identity Record are exhaustive. The scroll-state and pending-asset LRUs are bounded. `MOUNTED_BODY_BY_KEY` is total. F905/F920 were left alone as instructed. **Class 3 (unbounded lifetime) produced exactly ONE hit in the whole territory — F1350** — because nearly every map here is keyed by the closed `OverlayKey` vocabulary; the leak is in the one place keyed by a MONOTONE COUNTER instead. That is the generalizable lesson of this pass.

F1502 | search-flow-camera | apps/mobile/src/screens/Search/hooks/use-search-structured-submit-owner.ts:141 vs use-search-session-origin-camera-runtime.ts:95-98 | FAILURE CLASS 1 — THE LIST ENTRY POINTS CANNOT CAPTURE AN ORIGIN AT ALL WHEN A SESSION IS ALREADY LIVE. `launchListSearchResults` deliberately writes `committedBounds: null` (correct, and well-argued: a list world is bounds-independent and carrying a viewport polluted the worldKey — sim-proven 2026-07-13). The origin runtime's capture arm requires `committed != null`; its only other arm is `else if (sessionOriginCameraRef.current == null && committed == null)`. So a list launch seeds the origin ONLY when the slot is empty.
